subject: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality tests & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Patterson <grace.patterson@adept-robotics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality tests & next steps

Hi Grace / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap of the call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Key goals you mentioned: high factual accuracy for KB-augmented responses, low hallucination on long-form instructions, and predictable latency for 2k token completions.
- You’re running initial POC with a hyperscaler endpoint and an in-house HF deployment; you asked for a side-by-side on hallucination rates and regression sensitivity on your critical prompts.

Next steps we proposed:
1) You share a seed set of eval prompts (n ~ 50) and any ground-truths — Grace said she’d share a CSV by EOD Monday.
2) We’ll run the seed set across three variants: Redwood-curated Llama-2x (quantized), Hyperscaler-large (as you have it), and your in-house HF latest. We’ll measure hallucination rate, factuality, and temperature sensitivity.
3) We’ll surface: per-prompt diffs, top hallucination categories, and a short README with recommended mitigations (prompt templates, retrieval thresholds, temperature/profile suggestions).

Attached: a suggested prompt CSV template and a sample comparison summary (redwood_comparison_summary.pdf) so you can see the expected deliverable.

Can you confirm you’ll share the CSV and any ground-truth labels by EOD Monday (2026-04-13)? If yes, we’ll aim to deliver preliminary results by Thu (2026-04-16).

Thanks — excited to help benchmark this with you.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_comparison_summary.pdf (summary example)
- prompt_template.csv (template)

From: Grace Patterson <grace.patterson@adept-robotics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@adept-robotics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality tests & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we’ll share the eval set this morning (attached). The CSV includes: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_answer (where applicable), and priority flag. We also included an initial run from our hyperscaler vendor for baseline.

A few clarifications for your run: 
- Please include a deterministic decoding run (temp=0) and a default sampling run (temp=0.7).
- If possible, return the full model log-prob sequences for the deterministic run so we can inspect calibration differences. If that’s not possible for OpenAPI constraints, a token-level score summary is fine.

We’ve attached the CSV (adept_eval_prompts_v1.csv) and our baseline.xlsx with vendor outputs. Looking forward to your results.

—Grace
Director, Applied AI
Adept Robotics

Attachments:
- adept_eval_prompts_v1.csv
- adept_eval_results_initial.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace Patterson <grace.patterson@adept-robotics.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@adept-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality tests & next steps

Hi Grace / Samir —

Thanks for sending the eval set and baseline. We’ve kicked off the runs and I wanted to share the test plan so everyone has visibility: 

Test plan (short):
- Models: Redwood-llama2x-quant (4-bit), Hyperscaler-large (as provided in your baseline), Adept-inhouse-latest (your HF checkpoint).
- Modes: deterministic (temp=0) and sampling (temp=0.7).
- Metrics: hallucination_rate (binary per response vs expected_answer where provided), factuality_score (0-1 by automated heuristics + spot-checking), avg_confidence (mean token log-prob), and response_stability (variance across 5 sampling seeds for sampled runs).
- Artifacts we’ll deliver: per-prompt CSV with outputs, per-prompt metric columns, a short summary PDF with top 10 hallucination cases + remediation suggestions.

Operational notes:
- We can provide token-level summary (avg log-prob per token) for the deterministic run — full sequence logs may be large; we’ll include the top-k low-confidence tokens per response.
- Run ETA: initial automated pass by EOD Wed (2026-04-15 PST). We’ll do a lightweight manual spot-check of the top 30 priority prompts and include commentary.

Marissa — we’ll need a quick sign-off on whether to include quantized vs non-quantized Redwood variants (adds ~4 hours). If you approve, we’ll include both and call out quantization impact.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: run configuration in internal CI (link shared), will attach results once complete.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace Patterson <grace.patterson@adept-robotics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality tests & next steps

Thanks Dev — please go ahead and include both quantized and non-quantized Redwood variants (include the delta in the summary). Grace / Samir — we’ll deliver the automated pass today and schedule a 30-min review on Fri (2026-04-17) to walk the results and remediation recommendations.

Grace — would 10am PT on Fri work for a short sync? If yes, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround team.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
